first.rationale: The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single onboarding fix plausibly moves both metrics; that makes simplify_onboarding the highest-leverage use of the one slot. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the reflexive answer to the competitor's entry pricing, but the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are exactly the cohort most likely to churn or reprice at renewal — memory_73 records acquisition and revenue lift but says nothing about retention or margin over time, so I will not spend the slot there. I am verifying memory_31 and memory_86 rather than the memory backing an action I am declining, because they are the load-bearing evidence for what I intend to do and they are suspiciously convergent: both claim onboarding/signup simplification lifts SMB activation, consolidated 40 days apart. If they trace to the same underlying experiment, my evidence base is one study, not two, and the apparent corroboration is an artifact of consolidation. I also want the original records to check baseline conditions — a day-12 and day-52 result may not transfer to a day-76 market where a competitor is actively pulling the same segment, and the current declines could be composition effects (worse-fit traffic) rather than a broken funnel, in which case removing friction would speed low-quality signups through rather than fix anything. Key downstream risk: memory_31's specific mechanism is cutting required signup fields, which removes the qualification and routing data that sales-assisted enterprise conversion depends on (memory_44). A win on activation could therefore quietly degrade pipeline quality — the exact metric the primary objective targets. So I scope this as a small guarded test: restrict field removal to the self-serve SMB path, leave the demo-request path untouched, and instrument qualified-pipeline and 30-day retention alongside activation so a hollow activation lift is detectable. If verification shows memory_31 and memory_86 are one source, or that the original lift was measured only on first-week activation with no revenue-quality follow-through, I would keep the test but tighten it further rather than scale up.

final.rationale: Verification resolved my main worry in a useful direction: exp_31 and exp_86 are genuinely distinct experiments with different mechanisms, not one study double-counted through consolidation. So the onboarding direction has two independent supports. But the records also separate the two mechanisms sharply on exactly the dimension the objective cares about, and that changes which version I run. exp_31 (cutting required signup fields) bought +9% activation at the cost of -1% 30-day retention, with qualified revenue up only +4% against a +15% signup lift — that gap means most of the extra signups were not qualified revenue, i.e. partly hollow volume. And it is the mechanism that strips the routing and qualification data the sales-assisted enterprise path (memory_44) depends on. exp_86 (shortening the onboarding flow) is strictly better shaped: +13% completion, time-to-value -2.1 days, and retention positive at +3%. It improves the funnel without removing information from it. So I commit the slot to onboarding-flow shortening and explicitly exclude signup field removal, even though both live under the same action label. This also targets both observed declines at once — completion -4% directly, activation -6% indirectly, since faster time-to-value feeds the first-meaningful-action effect in memory_91. I am declining promotional pricing despite it being the direct counter to the competitor: memory_73 reports acquisition and revenue lift but carries no retention or margin figure, and the one inherited record I can now see in full that chased volume (exp_31) showed precisely the hollow-volume pattern discounting would amplify in the price-sensitive segment. Remaining uncertainty I am not resolving this week: exp_86 was run at day 52 under different competitive conditions, and neither record tells me whether current declines are a broken funnel or worse-fit inbound traffic. If it is composition, faster onboarding moves poorly-fit accounts through quicker and completion rises while qualified revenue does not. So I run this as a standard experiment on the self-serve path with the enterprise demo-request path untouched, and I gate the read on qualified pipeline and 30-day retention alongside completion and activation. A completion lift without the revenue-quality follow-through is a negative result, not a win, and I will treat it as one rather than scaling.
